rules.title: Built-in primitive scalar types
rules.statement: The language has primitive scalar types: void, bool, char, the floats f32/f64, and the integers i8/u8, i16/u16, i24/u24, i32/u32, i56/u56, i64/u64, i128/u128, isize/usize. Each is a distinct type identified by its keyword name.
rules.divergence: A: extra fixed-width widths i24/u24/i56/u56 and 128-bit i128/u128 beyond Rust's standard set.

rules.title: str defaults to &[u8] fat-slice shape
rules.statement: The `str` keyword resolves to the fat-pointer slice form `Slice<u8>` (the &[u8] shape) by default; in a context that explicitly permits an unsized result (e.g. a `T: ?Sized` turbofish position) it resolves to the unsized `[u8]` form so `&T` routes to the same Slice<u8> ABI without double-wrapping.
rules.uncertainty: str modeled as u8 slice rather than a distinct str primitive; unsized vs fat-slice choice is context-driven via unsized_ok_.

rules.title: Type-alias name resolution shadowing order
rules.statement: A bare type name N resolves to a 0-arg type alias by probing in order: (1) the current package's own alias `pkg::N`, (2) the bare/unqualified alias N, (3) aliases from wildcard-imported packages. The current package's alias thus shadows a same-named imported/stdlib alias (Rust scoping).

rules.title: Bare generic struct name with all-default params instantiates defaults
rules.statement: A bare struct name N (written without `<...>`) referring to a generic struct whose every type parameter has a default resolves to the defaulted instantiation `N<d0, d1, ...>`, where each default may reference earlier defaults via substitution. If any parameter lacks a default, the bare name resolves to the uninstantiated struct type.

rules.title: Type-name lookup precedence across namespaces
rules.statement: An unqualified type name resolves with precedence: primitive keyword > in-scope generic type parameter > type alias > struct > datatype > enum; the first match wins. An unresolved name yields no type.

rules.title: Struct is a move type unless Copy
rules.statement:
A struct-typed value is a move type (its source slot is invalidated on by-value use and dropped on scope exit) unless the struct implements Copy. Copy holds either unconditionally or conditionally (e.g. `impl Copy for Pin

`), the latter requiring every recorded copy-relevant type-argument position to hold a non-move (Copy) type.

rules.title: Enum is a move type iff droppable
rules.statement: An enum is a move type iff it has a user `impl Drop` or carries a droppable payload field; a C-like enum or one whose payloads are all Copy is non-move.

rules.title: Generic type parameter is move unless bounded Copy
rules.statement: A type parameter T is treated as a move type within a generic body unless its bounds include `Copy`, in which case T is provably Copy (Copy and Drop are mutually exclusive) and by-value use of `x: T` does not move. Only an explicit Copy bound makes T non-move; otherwise the conservative move classification holds.

rules.title: Owning heap pointers are move types
rules.statement: Owning heap-backed types are move types: an owning `Box<dyn Trait>`, an owning `Box<[T]>` slice, and an owning `Box<Foo>` custom-DST each own heap data and are non-Copy, hence move. The corresponding borrowed forms (`&dyn`, `&[T]`) are Copy-like and not move types.
